**ghz4.** Over 240 daily snapshots of real ibm_fez calibration data, a perfect tracker would have gained 0.2 % over the best fixed setting for ghz4 (arm 5, Z-R); the best setting changed significantly 25 times (26 epochs, median length 8 days; 72 raw argmax flips, ambiguous-day fraction 0.61). eps-greedy had the lowest dynamic pseudo-regret, 2.03 [1.29, 4.07], against 4.46 for the everything-on default and 0.37 for the static oracle (seeds 0–1, tuned on the same seeds).

**ghz8.** Over 240 daily snapshots of real ibm_fez calibration data, a perfect tracker would have gained 0.1 % over the best fixed setting for ghz8 (arm 5, Z-R); the best setting changed significantly 18 times (19 epochs, median length 7 days; 42 raw argmax flips, ambiguous-day fraction 0.49). eps-greedy had the lowest dynamic pseudo-regret, 3.21 [2.07, 5.59], against 10.20 for the everything-on default and 0.22 for the static oracle (seeds 0–1, tuned on the same seeds).

**grover3.** Over 240 daily snapshots of real ibm_fez calibration data, a perfect tracker would have gained 0.1 % over the best fixed setting for grover3 (arm 5, Z-R); the best setting changed significantly 5 times (6 epochs, median length 26 days; 20 raw argmax flips, ambiguous-day fraction 0.53). eps-greedy had the lowest dynamic pseudo-regret, 3.36 [1.98, 7.36], against 15.69 for the everything-on default and 0.11 for the static oracle (seeds 0–1, tuned on the same seeds).

**qaoa6.** Over 240 daily snapshots the best mitigation setting for qaoa6 was stationary: the drift value is 0.0 % (a fixed setting chosen once is within 0.0 % of a perfect tracker), with 0 raw argmax flips and an ambiguous-day fraction of 0.01. eps-greedy had the lowest dynamic pseudo-regret, 3.44 [2.18, 4.68], against 14.27 for the everything-on default and 0.00 for the static oracle (seeds 0–8, tuned on the same seeds).

**qft3.** Over 240 daily snapshots of real ibm_fez calibration data, a perfect tracker would have gained 0.0 % over the best fixed setting for qft3 (arm 5, Z-R); the best setting changed significantly 5 times (6 epochs, median length 34 days; 34 raw argmax flips, ambiguous-day fraction 0.65). eps-greedy had the lowest dynamic pseudo-regret, 2.06 [1.20, 4.95], against 3.80 for the everything-on default and 0.07 for the static oracle (seeds 0–8, tuned on the same seeds).

**Proxy validation (per day).** ghz4: the mirror score picked the forward-best arm on 46 % of 240 days (median Spearman 0.88, median forward regret of the mirror pick 1 % of the worst arm's). grover3: the mirror score picked the forward-best arm on 94 % of 240 days (median Spearman 0.93, median forward regret of the mirror pick 0 % of the worst arm's). qft3: the mirror score picked the forward-best arm on 29 % of 240 days (median Spearman 0.62, median forward regret of the mirror pick 8 % of the worst arm's).

**Drivers.** ghz4: a multinomial logistic fit of the best arm on chain cz error, readout error, T1 and T2 reaches cross-validated accuracy 0.80 against a majority rate of 0.80; 11 of 25 significant switches fall within a day of a chip-wide recalibration (base rate 0.51). ghz8: a multinomial logistic fit of the best arm on chain cz error, readout error, T1 and T2 reaches cross-validated accuracy 0.91 against a majority rate of 0.91; 11 of 18 significant switches fall within a day of a chip-wide recalibration (base rate 0.51). grover3: a multinomial logistic fit of the best arm on chain cz error, readout error, T1 and T2 reaches cross-validated accuracy 0.96 against a majority rate of 0.95; 2 of 5 significant switches fall within a day of a chip-wide recalibration (base rate 0.51). qaoa6: 0 of 0 significant switches fall within a day of a chip-wide recalibration (base rate 0.51). qft3: a multinomial logistic fit of the best arm on chain cz error, readout error, T1 and T2 reaches cross-validated accuracy 0.91 against a majority rate of 0.92; 2 of 5 significant switches fall within a day of a chip-wide recalibration (base rate 0.51).
